title: Travel Protection Plans: Terms on Giving Up Cover After the Free-Look Period
content:
After the free-look period the policyholder may still give up Travel Protection Plans cover, and the plan's mid-term share of the unearned premium is returned.

Unearned premium is measured by the whole days of cover remaining out of the whole days of cover bought, counted from the day after the cancellation takes effect.

Nothing is returned on a plan whose mid-term share is zero, and nothing is returned once any claim has been filed under the policy, whatever the plan.

The policy fee and any cancel-for-any-reason upgrade premium are never part of the unearned premium.

Cover ends at the moment the cancellation is confirmed, and an incident occurring afterwards is not covered even where the journey continues.

A cancelled policy is never reinstated. A traveller who changes their mind buys fresh cover, subject to the underwriting rules as they then stand.

## The proportion worked through

Suppose, hypothetically, a certificate bought for 60 whole days of cover, cancelled with 24 whole days of cover remaining when counted from the day after the cancellation takes effect. The unearned proportion is 24 out of 60, which is two fifths. On premium of 500.00 USD other than the policy fee and other than any cancel-for-any-reason upgrade premium, the unearned premium is two fifths of 500.00 USD, which is 200.00 USD. The plan's mid-term share is then taken of that 200.00 USD, and it is that share, not the whole unearned figure, that is returned.

Two circumstances stop the calculation before it begins. Where the plan's mid-term share is zero, nothing is returned however many days remain. Where any claim has been filed under the policy, nothing is returned whatever the plan and whatever the days.

## What ends and what does not

Cover ends at the moment of confirmation. A journey that continues after that moment continues uninsured, and an incident occurring then is not covered. The certificate is not brought back afterwards: fresh cover is a fresh purchase, judged by the underwriting rules standing at that later time.
